# AAPL — Quantitative Fundamental Attractiveness Report

**Decision date:** 2026-06-05 | **Latest filing:** Q2 FY2026 (period_end 2026-03-28) | **Latest price:** 2026-06-04

---

## 1. Revenue, Earnings, Margin & Cash-Flow Trajectory

Apple's most recent quarter (Q2 2026-03-28) delivered revenue of $111.18B and diluted EPS of $2.01. On a YoY basis the business is growing solidly: revenue +16.6%, EPS +21.8%, net income +19.4%, and gross profit +22.1%. Operating cash flow likewise rose +19.8% YoY to $28.70B.

The QoQ comparisons appear alarming at first glance — revenue −22.7%, EPS −29.2%, operating cash flow −46.8% — but this is consistent with Apple's seasonal pattern where the December holiday quarter (Q1 FY, here 2025-12-27 at $143.76B / $2.84 EPS) is the cyclical peak. The sequential decline is normal seasonality, not an inflection.

Margins are expanding. The Q2 gross margin was 49.3% ($54.78B / $111.18B) versus 48.2% a year prior (implied from $44.87B / $95.36B in Q2 2025-03-29). The trailing net margin ratio stands at 27.2% and operating margin at 32.6% — both at or near the upper end of their respective 12-month ranges (net margin 0.2–0.3; operating margin not explicitly ranged but the latest is the highest in the data set).

**Free cash flow is unavailable** in the data set; operating cash flow is the primary cash-generation proxy. The $28.70B quarterly OCF (up 19.8% YoY) and the prior-quarter $53.92B demonstrate robust and consistent cash generation across the cycle.

**TTM cannot be computed:** the growth panel states the TTM period is incomplete due to a fiscal-quarter gap (the four available quarters are Q2–Q1–Q3–Q2 rather than four contiguous quarters). Any trailing-twelve-month sum would be unreliable and is therefore not cited.

## 2. Earnings Quality & Balance-Sheet Resilience

Earnings quality appears high. Net income translates closely to operating cash flow: $29.58B in net income vs. $28.70B OCF in the latest quarter (OCF-to-NI ratio ≈ 0.97x), indicating earnings are backed by real cash. Gross margins are expanding YoY, and operating income of $35.88B represents a healthy 32.3% operating margin on revenue — again at the top of the recent range.

The balance sheet has materially strengthened over the five-quarter window:

| Quarter | Total Debt | Total Equity | D/E |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-12-28 | $94.80B | $66.76B | 1.42x |
| 2025-03-29 | $92.20B | $66.80B | 1.38x |
| 2025-06-28 | $91.80B | $65.83B | 1.39x |
| 2025-12-27 | $88.50B | $88.19B | 1.00x |
| **2026-03-28** | **$82.70B** | **$106.49B** | **0.78x** |

Debt has been reduced by $12.1B over five quarters while equity has expanded by $39.7B, likely driven by retained earnings and buyback-related accounting. The current debt-to-equity of 0.777 is the lowest in the series. Total assets of $371.08B with total liabilities of $264.59B leave ample room. The ROE of 1.151 (115%) — while inflated by the relatively modest equity base — reflects exceptional profitability on shareholders' capital.

## 3. Valuation Versus Own History

The current PE of 37.39x sits in the **upper half** of the trailing 12-month range of 30.3x–43.1x. The peak was 43.1x (reached around late 2025), and the trough was 30.3x. The latest reading has recovered from a local low of 31.9x on 2026-03-31, implying the market has re-rated the stock upward over the past two months alongside the strong Q2 print.

P/B of 43.0x is **below** its 12-month range of 38.3x–65.0x, reflecting the substantial equity growth (rising denominator). Price-to-sales of 10.15x is rich in absolute terms. The earnings yield of 2.7% compares unfavourably to the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.47% — a 177 bp gap — meaning investors are paying a premium over risk-free for the growth and quality profile.

The margin trajectory supports the premium partially: net margin has expanded from 24.3% (mid-2025) to 27.2% currently, and ROE has compressed from 1.5x to 1.15x not because of deteriorating returns but because the equity base grew sharply. This is a positive-earnings-quality signal.

## 4. Price Context

AAPL closed at $311.23 on 2026-06-04, near the 12-month high of $316.94 and well above the 12-month low of $195.07. The quarterly return of +19.6% (from $260.29 on 2026-03-05) followed a prior-quarter decline of −9.0% and a +20.0% quarter before that. The stock is in a volatile but broadly upward channel, and the recent rally has pushed the price back toward the top of the range.

The +19.6% quarterly move appears to have **already reflected** the strong Q2 YoY growth. With PE now back to 37.4x after compressing to 31.9x in late March, much of the re-rating may be priced in.

## 5. Macro & Sentiment Overlays

**Rates:** The 10-year yield at 4.47% and the 2-year at 4.05% indicate a positively sloped curve (T10Y2Y = +0.42%). The Fed funds rate at 3.63% is slightly lower than yields, suggesting the market prices modest further easing. However, the 10-year yield has risen 35 bp over the quarter, and Apple's 2.7% earnings yield is now significantly below the risk-free rate. This is a **valuation headwind** — a sustained high-rate regime compresses what investors will pay for growth.

**Volatility:** VIX at 15.4 (down from 25.5 three months prior) reflects a benign risk environment. This supports elevated multiples but also signals complacency risk.

**Oil:** WTI at $96.83/bbl is elevated and has been volatile ($83–$114 range). As a consumer-facing company with hardware supply chains sensitive to energy costs, sustained high oil is a modest margin headwind — though Apple's expanding margins suggest effective cost management.

**Sentiment:** News sentiment mean of 0.255 over 90 days (507 articles) is mildly positive. Recent readings cluster in the 0.0–0.6 range with occasional negative dips. Sentiment is not extreme enough to be contrarian in either direction.

**Initial claims** ticked up to 225K (latest week 2026-05-30), the highest in the 13-week series, potentially signalling a softening labour market — a demand risk for premium consumer electronics.

## 6. Strongest Quantitative Upside & Downside

**Upside:**
- YoY EPS growth of +21.8% on expanding margins (gross margin 49.3% vs. ~47% a year prior) demonstrates pricing power and mix improvement.
- Balance-sheet deleveraging (D/E from 1.42x to 0.78x) creates optionality for buybacks or investment, and the cash-generation engine (OCF $28.70B in a seasonally weak quarter) is robust.
- If margins sustain at 27%+ net and the multiple re-rates back toward the 43x peak seen in late 2025, there is valuation upside — but this requires continued earnings beats.

**Downside:**
- Earnings yield of 2.7% vs. 10-year yield of 4.47% leaves the stock vulnerable to any further rate increases or failure to grow into the multiple.
- PE at 37.4x is above the 12-month median (~35x); a mean-reversion to 31–33x on any earnings disappointment implies 12–17% downside.
- Seasonal Q1 (Dec) is the earnings peak; if the upcoming FY Q3 and Q4 show normal sequential declines without YoY acceleration, the premium multiple may compress.
- Jobless claims rising to 225K and oil near $97 represent macro risks to consumer demand and input costs.

## 7. Provisional Conclusion

Apple's business fundamentals are solid: double-digit YoY revenue and earnings growth, expanding margins, strong cash generation, and a rapidly strengthening balance sheet. However, the **quantitative valuation is stretched relative to own history and to prevailing interest rates**. The 37.4x PE — above the 12-month median and with an earnings yield 177 bp below the 10-year Treasury — prices in continued growth and margin expansion. The recent 19.6% quarterly price rally and PE re-rating from 31.9x to 37.4x suggest much of the near-term positive has been captured.

**Provisional quantitative stance: Fairly valued to modestly overvalued.** The business trajectory is attractive, but the entry price already reflects it. Fundamental attractiveness is neutral — high-quality business, but the cost of admission is elevated versus the company's own valuation history and versus the risk-free alternative.

# AAPL — Qualitative Franchise Assessment
**Decision date: 2026-06-05**

---

## 1. Business / Franchise Read

Apple's franchise rests on three interlocking pillars: an installed base exceeding 2.5 billion active devices, a tightly integrated hardware-software-services ecosystem, and a capital-return machine that has returned over $700 billion to shareholders since 2012. The business model is hybrid: transactional hardware sales (iPhone ~50-52% of revenue) bring customers into the ecosystem, where high-margin recurring services revenue (gross margins ~70-77% vs. ~36-39% for products) compounds lifetime value.

Services revenue reached $96.1 billion in FY2025 (14% YoY growth), with the segment now exceeding $109 billion on a full-year basis per multiple sources. This mix shift is structural, not cyclical — Services grew from roughly 22% of sales to a materially larger share over recent years, pulling blended gross margins upward. The ecosystem exhibits exceptional retention: approximately 85% of iPhone sales come from existing owners upgrading, and customer retention is estimated at 92% — well above Samsung's ~77%.

Apple's competitive moat is deep but not impregnable. The company dominates the premium smartphone segment (global unit share ~20% but the lion's share of industry profit), holds ~58% US smartphone OS share, and ~69% in Japan. The 88% US teen iPhone ownership rate (Piper Sandler spring 2025 survey) signals durable demand-pull for the next decade. Custom silicon (M-series, A-series) has materially strengthened the Mac and iPhone value propositions, and the "build-not-buy" acquisition philosophy — small capability tuck-ins, not large mergers — preserves engineering culture and integration control.

Capital allocation is aggressive and shareholder-friendly: $90.7 billion in buybacks in FY2025 alone, a fresh $100 billion authorization announced in 2026, and a 4% dividend increase. At ~$110 billion in annual operating cash flow (FY2023 figure; FCF estimated at ~$99 billion annually per recent sources), the return program is roughly self-funding. Share count has declined ~40% since 2013, mechanically boosting EPS.

---

## 2. Recent Developments (Dated)

**Q2 FY2026 earnings (reported April 30, 2026):** Revenue of $111.2 billion (+17% YoY), iPhone revenue +22%, Services revenue of $30.98 billion for the quarter, gross margin expanded to 49.3% from 48.2%. The $100 billion buyback authorization and 4% dividend increase accompanied the print. Two consecutive quarters of 20%+ EPS growth were cited (2026-06-04, Benzinga/2026-05-23, Motley Fool).

**CEO transition announced April 20, 2026:** Tim Cook stepping down; John Ternus (SVP Hardware Engineering, 25-year Apple veteran) named successor. This is the first leadership change in 15 years. Ternus led hardware engineering on iPhone, Vision Pro, Apple Silicon, and the iPhone 17 lineup (2026-05-22, swotpal.com).

**WWDC 2026 (June 8-12) — imminent catalyst:** Morgan Stanley sees potential for a rally to $440 if Apple successfully unveils an improved Siri and Apple Intelligence strategy; UBS remains skeptical on the broader AI narrative. A rebuilt AI-powered Siri running on a Google Gemini model (with Apple paying Google roughly $1 billion annually) is the marquee expected announcement. Bank of America raised its price target to $380 (2026-06-04, Benzinga; 2026-06-02, Motley Fool).

**Stock performance:** Apple rose 15% in May, broke out above $300 to all-time highs, and is now extending with strong relative strength ahead of WWDC (2026-06-03, Motley Fool; 2026-06-03, CNBC).

**India supply-chain shift:** India now accounts for 25% of global iPhone production (up from <5% four years ago). Apple is targeting majority of US-bound iPhone production from India by end of 2026 (2026-05-22, swotpal.com).

**Berkshire Hathaway positioning:** Greg Abel (new CEO since January 2026) maintains Apple as the largest holding at ~20.7% of Berkshire's $330 billion portfolio, alongside a tripling of the Alphabet position. Apple is one of three holdings comprising 45.7% of the portfolio (2026-05-31, 2026-05-23, Motley Fool).

---

## 3. Material Risks and Offsets

**Regulatory — three-front war (HIGH):** The Supreme Court rejected Apple's App Store appeal on April 6, 2026, requiring external payment links — this could reduce App Store commission revenue by an estimated $2-4 billion annually. The EU fined Apple €500 million for DMA non-compliance and is intensifying enforcement requiring third-party app stores and alternative payments. A DOJ antitrust suit is ongoing. All three target Services economics — the company's margin engine.

*Offset:* Services revenue is diversifying beyond App Store commissions (iCloud, AppleCare, Apple Pay, subscriptions), and privacy positioning increasingly aligns with global regulatory direction on data protection.

**China structural pressure (MEDIUM-HIGH):** Huawei's resurgence, Beijing's AI regulations requiring government approval for LLM commercial use, and Apple Intelligence not yet at full feature parity in mainland China. Greater China represents ~18% of revenue. Recent Q1 FY2026 showed 38% China growth, but competitive dynamics remain challenging (2026-05-22, swotpal.com; 2026-05-21, businessmodelanalyst.com).

*Offset:* Geographic diversification is underway; Americas at 43% of revenue provides ballast.

**Tariff / trade policy (MEDIUM):** Apple has paid $3.3 billion in cumulative tariffs ($800M in Q1 FY2026 alone). New 10-15% blanket tariffs under Section 122 could add $100-$350 to iPhone 17 retail prices. India diversification helps but Trump has signaled opposition to Indian manufacturing as well (2026-05-22, swotpal.com; 2026-05-21, businessmodelanalyst.com).

**AI execution gap (MEDIUM):** Over half of eligible US iPhone owners have not activated Apple Intelligence features. Siri's major upgrade was delayed to spring 2026 due to "significant engineering problems." The WWDC Siri/AI reveal is a make-or-break moment for the narrative; UBS remains skeptical (2026-05-22, swotpal.com; 2026-06-04, Benzinga).

*Offset:* The 2.5-billion-device installed base is a distribution advantage no competitor matches. Bank of America projects $15-30 billion in AI-related revenue by FY2030 (2026-05-30, Motley Fool).

**Leadership transition (LOW-MEDIUM):** First CEO change in 15 years, during a period of regulatory war and AI catch-up. Execution risk exists, though Ternus is a deeply embedded insider (2026-05-22, swotpal.com).

---

## 4. Qualitative Assessment

**POSITIVE on fundamental attractiveness — with caveats.**

Apple's franchise quality remains among the highest in global equities. The ecosystem moat — 2.5 billion devices, ~92% retention, ~85% repeat iPhone purchases, Services growing at 14%+ at 70%+ gross margins — is structurally durable and self-reinforcing. The capital-return program is disciplined and nearly fully self-funding. The installed base is a genuine platform for AI monetization, even if current adoption lags expectations.

The financial trajectory is accelerating: two consecutive quarters of 20%+ EPS growth, 17% revenue growth, gross margin expansion, and a fresh $100B buyback. The stock breaking to all-time highs reflects improving fundamental momentum, not mere narrative.

However, the franchise faces its most challenging external environment in years: a simultaneous three-front regulatory assault on App Store economics, tariff uncertainty that could meaningfully impact iPhone pricing, and a China market where local competitors are gaining ground. The AI narrative is the near-term swing factor — a strong WWDC could validate the monetization thesis, while disappointment risks a valuation reset given the premium multiple.

The leadership transition introduces incremental uncertainty but is not a franchise-damaging event given Ternus's deep product and operational credentials. Net-net: the structural franchise supports continued fundamental attractiveness, but the risk surface is wider than at any point in recent memory, and the stock's premium valuation leaves limited margin of safety against adverse regulatory or AI outcomes.

---

unsupported_claims: Quant report states prior-year gross margin was '48.2% (implied from $44.87B / $95.36B in Q2 2025-03-29)' but 44.87/95.36 = 47.05%, not 48.2%. sources_cited.excerpt: Morgan Stanley believes Apple's WWDC 2026 (June 8-12) could trigger a major AI narrative shift for the stock, with potential for a rally to $440… UBS remains skeptical
Apple stock rose 15% in May driven by market confidence in AI and strong iPhone sales (up 22% year-over-year)
Supreme Court rejected Apple's App Store appeal (April 6), requiring external payment links. Combined with EU DMA and DOJ suit, Apple faces a three-front regulatory battle
Services revenue grew 14% year-over-year to $96.1 billion in fiscal 2025… iPhone sales remain the cornerstone, with 231 million units sold in fiscal 2025

India now accounts for 25% of global iPhone production (up from <5% four years ago). Apple is targeting majority of US-bound iPhone production from India by end of 2026, partially offsetting the $3.3B cumulative tariff cost
Over half of eligible U.S. iPhone owners have not activated AI features… Siri's major upgrade was delayed to spring 2026 due to 'significant engineering problems'
$90.7 billion in share repurchases in FY2025… Apple has repurchased over $700 billion of its own stock over the past decade
